title: Eichenberg & Associates — Change management for mid-market go-lives

gap.heading: Your SI will get the system live. Who's making sure your people can run the operation on day one?
paragraphs: Training completion tells you who clicked through. It doesn't tell you who can do the job on day one.
The SI plan covers cutover; people readiness is a line item for training sessions. Status reports are green, but you can't see whether operations is ready.
gap.closing: The SI brings system expertise. We bring people expertise.

who.heading: Mid-market companies with a go-live date
who.lead: Where the sponsor is reachable and a firm our size is the right fit.

facts.label: Company size
facts.text: $100M–$1B in revenue. 500–5,000 employees, with 250+ affected by the go-live.

facts.label: Industries
facts.text: Primary depth: insurance. Also manufacturing, pharmaceuticals and automotive.

facts.label: Sponsor
facts.text: An executive owns the go-live and is reachable. No large consulting firm already running change.

facts.label: Initiative
facts.text: Fixed go-live date and a seven-figure program. ERP and HR rollouts, merger integrations, facility openings.

approach.heading: Phased OCM leadership. Fixed fee by phase.

phases.name: Prepare
phases.text: Role Readiness modules get SMEs, the project team, managers and sponsors ready before Systems Integrator (SI) design sessions start.

phases.name: Act
phases.text: Readiness work through build and test, with associate production inside the engagement and a Readiness Assessment at 90 days or less.

phases.name: Sustain
phases.text: Go-live plus 90 days: a check-in on adoption, and planning for the next initiative.

approach.footnote: Sponsor access and go/no-go criteria in every contract. A 90-day check-in after every engagement.

partners.heading: When adoption stalls, the client blames the implementation. A readiness check protects your go-live and your relationship.
partners.text: Offer OCM without building a practice. You cover the system; we cover the people. Subcontracted anchor lead, or white-label assessments and modules.
